items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: I played on the bills with Jolson.

ctx.x: What was his name again? Carter?

Earl Carter. Yeah. A Chicago drummer. He filled in for two weeks. And Spobara comes up and takes his place. This man knew that that's all the way we used him for two weeks. And we did pretty good at the Del Abbey. Then Harry James buys an entrance in the Casino Gardens with Aikenbar and Reeves. And he approaches us and offers us $75 a week to play in the Casino Gardens. We went and played the Casino Gardens. That was Kinzen Clock. And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself.…

Over the Shilly cafe was made June. I mean March April and May And in June We work at the lab it could be in July It worked there to the last last part of December with shields This is the band that got the name original Dixieland jazz band Because prior to that we had no building We were building at this place as the original Dixieland jazz band by Harry James Cards were given out there may have been notices in the paper. I don't know now They had many musicians who went and played at this place that we left at…
